<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

#35573 enabled the fused QK-norm and QK-norm+RoPE paths on ROCm, but the kernels behind them still don't build on all models. `elementwise/qknorm.cuh` fails outright, and `diffusion/qknorm_rope.cuh` fails for neox instantiations. Non-neox rope is the one case that already worked, which is why FLUX.2 saw the benefit of #35573 and MiniMax H3 did not. These compile failures do not keep the model from running, it's just slower.

This PR removes two dead CUDA includes in qknorm.cuh, and on ROCm pins the shuffle width to the kernel's 32-lane sub-group instead of letting HIP default it to the physical wave64. With both fixed, MiniMax-H3's QK-norm paths accept ROCm.

Without these changes neither of the kernels work on ROCm. Theser are necessary for eager / compile mode parity.

CUDA is unaffected. The shuffle change is behind `#ifndef USE_ROCM` and the dropped includes were dead.
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications

- `elementwise/qknorm.cuh` carried `cuda_bf16.h` / `cuda_fp16.h` as dead includes, which hipcc cannot find ("fatal error: 'cuda_bf16.h' file not found"). The file reaches the GPU only through `impl/norm.cuh` and the `runtime.cuh` macro shims, both of which hipcc builds, so the includes can just go.

-  `__shfl_sync(kActiveMask, ...)` passes a `uint32_t` mask, and HIP static_asserts `sizeof(MaskT) == 8`. On ROCm this now calls `__shfl(..., partner_lane, device::kWarpThreads)` instead.  `device::kWarpThreads` is 32u unconditionally, so the kernel indexes lanes in 32-wide logical warps, while HIP defaults the shuffle width to the physical wave64. `partner_lane` is an index inside that 32-lane sub-group, so the width has to be explicit.

- minimax_h3.py gated `_apply_qk_norm` and `_use_fused_qknorm_rope` on `current_platform.is_cuda()`. Both now accept ROCm, which is what reaches the two kernels above. MiniMax uses is_neox=True, the instantiation that did not
build.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

For testing, using MiniMax-H3. The output changes slightly (exactly 1 BF16 ULP) as expected by the rope kernel. Enabling torch.compile would change it as well. No artifacts present.

Command:
```
sglang generate \
    --model-path MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-H3 \
    --ulysses-degree 8 --ring-degree 1 --num-gpus 8 \
    --num-inference-steps 50 \
    --dit-cpu-offload False --dit-layerwise-offload False \
    --text-encoder-cpu-offload False --image-encoder-cpu-offload False \
    --offload-during-compile False --vae-cpu-offload False \
    --warmup-mode request --warmup-steps 50 \
    --vae-precision bf16 --image-encoder-precision bf16 \
    --output-path /outputs/minimax_h3.pr1 \
    --prompt 'A cat flying through the universe on a broom, playing rap music from his boombox' \
    --seed 42 \
    --config /outputs/minimax_h3.pr1/config.json \
    --perf-dump-path /outputs/minimax_h3.pr1/perf/pr1.json"
```

thanks @avjves ! the shuffle fix reads right to me.
one question on the gating: the rope site keeps `can_use_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`, but this one only has the dtype/stride conditions, and `fused_inplace_qknorm` goes straight to `_jit_qknorm_module` with no fallback , so a JIT failure here raises rather than degrading to eager. is head_dim=128 / bf16 the only shape this model reaches, or would a `can_use_...` guard be worth adding alongside?

Good call, added!
Currently nothing would break if it was not there, but the `can_use_` should be used to gracefully handle any JIT compilation errors any machine might have,
